verdict.rationale: The docs touch on parts of the security picture. They state that skills can bundle optional scripts alongside SKILL.md instructions. They describe a review process for public plugins: submission, resolving automated findings, and approval before publishing. The curated marketplace catalog carries installation and authentication policies. On data, Sign in with ChatGPT shares only name, email and profile picture, and grants no data access or automatic action approval. There is no consolidated security-posture statement: nothing documents execution limits or sandboxing for skill scripts, the trust model for third-party or experimental skills installed outside review, or telemetry collection. Missing for 10: documented execution boundaries or sandboxing for skill scripts, an explicit trust model for unreviewed third-party skills, telemetry and data-collection disclosure, and independent corroboration.
